Measure pyridyl ketone m66 at 2/1, predicted V1/V2 21.74/61.47 mL. Its loading matches the recently measured 5/1 experiment, which gave 47.37/119.31 after a large completion underestimate. A stronger-eluent anchor tests whether the new molecular correction extends appropriately across solvent ratios.

Measure ethyl nicotinate m90 at 2/1, predicted 23.27/58.54 mL. Together with selected m66 at 2/1 and pending m90 at 10/1, this tests transfer between pyridyl ester and ketone environments and constrains the location of the predicted retention rise. The selected sample is 100 uL; the existing pure-EA and pending m90 rows use 150 uL.

Measure methylquinoline at 10/1, predicted 42.23/77.96 mL, preserving the loading of its measured 2/1 experiment. The 2/1 result, 16.29/33.41, closely matched its acquisition prediction. This tests whether accurate baseline transfer also predicts solvent sensitivity, after quinoline showed a large historical underestimate at 10/1.

Measure amino ester m72 at 20/1 with a 50-uL sample in 200-uL DCM, predicted 25.58/98.35 mL. The measured 20/1 row uses 150 uL and gave 29.26/109.68; the measured 10/1 row uses 50 uL and gave 12.85/32.50. This controlled loading contrast separates a solvent-driven completion jump from a sample-amount contribution.

Measure benzyl-substituted acetoacetate m78 at 20/1, predicted 32.07/53.26 mL. Its loading matches the recent 50/1 experiment, measured 56.96/97.46 after a 40.18-mL completion underestimate. The interior ratio constrains where the retention increase occurs; the existing 10/1 anchor uses a larger sample.

Measure aromatic diketone m178 at 20/1, predicted 24.64/57.14 mL. Its measured 5/1 and 50/1 anchors, 6.03/18.17 and 44.91/98.73, have identical loading. This clean interior comparison tests response curvature for separated aromatic carbonyls.

Measure methoxyethyl acrylate at 10/1, predicted 8.93/15.63 mL, preserving the loading of its recent 5/1 experiment. That experiment measured 12.76/21.52 after a large completion overestimate. The current prediction decreases at weaker eluent; measuring it distinguishes an actual recorded reversal from an unsupported consequence of retraining.

Measure 1-phenyl-1-propanol at 5/1, predicted 14.92/24.92 mL, with the same loading as its measured 10/1 experiment. The 10/1 result, 22.46/33.08, rejected the predicted transfer of very early benzylic-alcohol elution. This second ratio constrains its solvent slope and the scope of the unusual 1-phenylethanol trajectory.

Measure 3-phenyl-1-propanol at 5/1, predicted 37.32/65.44 mL. Its loading matches the measured 10/1 experiment, 51.71/94.93. The recent 1/1 result was much earlier than predicted, though at lower loading. This interior point tests the predicted steep primary-alcohol response and complements the secondary-alcohol measurement.

Measure para-nitrobenzophenone at 50/1, predicted 15.44/86.86 mL. Its loading matches the measured 20/1 experiment, 4.78/57.02. This tests whether onset remains relatively early as completion increases, or whether both endpoints shift together. The large V1 quantile width is a model-behavior flag, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

Introduce para-acetoxybenzaldehyde m28 at 10/1, predicted 20.48/44.44 mL. This bridges aromatic aldehydes and ester-containing molecules through an uncovered acetoxy substituent. Recent ether/carbonyl and acrylate outcomes motivate testing local oxygen connectivity rather than assuming an oxygen-count correction. Structural references have different loading conditions.

Introduce methyl-substituted tetralone m63 at 20/1, predicted 5.26/18.50 mL, with maximum observed similarity 0.394. Related cyclic ketone m179 measured 6.13/23.54 at this ratio. The label tests transfer to a fused-ring and methyl-substitution environment where carbonyl accessibility and conformation may matter; the direction of those effects remains untested.

Introduce chalcone m165 at 20/1, predicted 8.26/21.48 mL. Related dibenzalacetone has measured anchors at 1/1 and 50/1 spanning 5.13/10.05 to 28.20/68.68. This tests whether changing carbonyl conjugation and aromatic placement alters solvent sensitivity as predicted, adding a useful bridge within the numerous aromatic carbonyl rows.

Introduce phosphorus-containing structure m202 at 5/1, predicted 7.29/18.39 mL, with 122.3 mg in 300-uL DCM. Its maximum observed similarity is 0.409. The supplied SMILES explicitly contains [P+], an unusual graph environment in this catalog. A label tests the modest predicted retention; actual speciation and counterion information are absent.

Measure methyl thioglycolate m96 at 20/1, predicted 21.35/54.75 mL. Its loading matches the measured 5/1 experiment, 9.59/12.50. Pending m96 at 50/1 predicts 30.36/79.69 with a larger sample. The interior anchor tests a strong predicted completion increase for a thiol/ester combination and helps interpret the pending weak-eluent result.

Measure methylenedioxy-substituted aliphatic aldehyde m59 at 10/1, predicted 16.26/29.40 mL. Its loading matches pending m59 at 50/1, predicted 51.89/84.38. The measured 1/1 anchor is 4.61/8.57 at a smaller sample volume. This supplies an interior constraint for the steep predicted response and tests transfer from directly aromatic ether/aldehyde environments.

hypotheses.content: The current predictions for m78, m178, m177 and m96 imply different solvent-response shapes and different relative movements of onset and completion. These predicted shapes may require local supervision beyond a molecular retention baseline.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Interior and endpoint-specific measurements can constrain interpolation and extrapolation across numerous condition rows without imposing one correction on both targets.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m78 and m178 interior labels support the predicted transitions, and do nitrobenzophenone and thioglycolate exhibit the predicted endpoint-specific increases?

hypotheses.content: The current model predicts similar substantial retention for the pyridyl ketone and ester at 2/1 and a steep methylquinoline response by 10/1. Transfer of these solvent responses across nitrogen environments remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected comparisons distinguish a learned nitrogen-containing molecular baseline from solvent sensitivity and carbonyl-context effects.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 2/1, are the pyridyl ketone and ester as similar and strongly retained as predicted, and does methylquinoline follow its predicted increase to 10/1?

hypotheses.content: The model's near invariance to sample amount may be inadequate for amino ester m72 at 20/1. A controlled sample-volume contrast can test whether loading contributes to its predicted late completion.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A loading contrast can prevent a sample-amount effect from being attributed entirely to solvent ratio, or establish that the sharp response persists at lower loading.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 20/1 and fixed DCM loading volume, does reducing sample volume from 150 to 50 uL materially change completion?

hypotheses.content: The model predicts substantially different 5/1 retention for benzylic secondary and distal primary alcohols. Additional matched-loading solvent comparisons may constrain transfer across hydroxyl environments.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Similar donor/acceptor counts do not determine identical silica interactions. Local response measurements can teach structural distinctions while limiting propagation of unusual onset predictions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do 1-phenyl-1-propanol and 3-phenyl-1-propanol follow their predicted 5/1 positions relative to their other measured ratios?

hypotheses.content: The model's oxygen-containing molecular transfers remain sensitive to connectivity, conjugation and ring environment. The predicted methoxyethyl-acrylate reversal and the predictions for acetoxybenzaldehyde, methyl tetralone, chalcone and m59 provide discriminating tests.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These labels can improve transfer among the catalog's many esters, ethers and carbonyls by supervising local chemical environments and response shapes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does methoxyethyl acrylate truly elute earlier at 10/1 than 5/1, and do the selected structural bridges follow their predicted retention patterns?

feedback_interpretation: The latest labels strengthen the case for selective interior measurements and weaken broad molecular corrections. Oxime at 20/1 measured 17.68/45.32, substantially below its acquisition prediction, continuing the earlier interior overestimate. The cyclopropyl keto ester and bromo acid likewise came below their predictions at 10/1. Conversely, mandelate at 10/1 measured 38.99/58.03, rejecting the predicted plateau. The amino ester measured slightly earlier at 10/1 than at 5/1 under matched loading, so a universal monotonic interpretation is inappropriate; its much later 20/1 completion still confounds ratio with loading and now warrants a controlled contrast. The pyridyl ketone's 47.37/119.31 result was the largest recent failure, whereas methylquinoline at 2/1 transferred accurately. This redirects nitrogen acquisition toward response shape and carbonyl context. The 1-phenyl-1-propanol label rejected transfer of the very early 1-phenylethanol prediction; the secondary-alcohol 5/1 measurements otherwise supported a structural contrast. Both acrylates finished earlier than predicted, especially methoxyethyl acrylate, weakening a generic ether-containing ester correction. Fused ether aldehyde and methoxybenzophenone predictions were comparatively close, so their measured regions receive lower priority. Naphthaldehyde at 50/1 did not support the predicted high onset and narrow interval; its inconsistent 20/1 anchor should not be generalized as a physical rule. CW outcomes additionally exposed underestimates in benzyl-substituted acetoacetate, bromo phenylacetate and cyanoacetophenone, while several alcohol and heterocycle predictions were overestimates. These are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The same 16 selections remain frozen. The pending batch emphasizes weak-eluent coverage, including ethyl nicotinate, thioglycolate, m59, phenol, aromatic esters and ethers. These supplements make several pending labels more interpretable through interior ratios, directly follow up the pyridyl-ketone failure, and resolve the amino ester loading confound. Matched-loading comparisons are used where available; structural comparisons and remaining loading differences are explicitly distinguished. Acetoxybenzaldehyde, methyl tetralone, chalcone and the phosphorus-containing graph expand support in useful chemical environments. The acrylate selection checks a predicted reversal after a large overestimate, and the alcohol selections constrain transfer of unusual onset behavior. Oxime, mandelate, bromo acid and cyclopropyl ester now have several informative anchors, so further nearby rows receive lower priority. Quantile widths and CW distances inform attention without being treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. V2 minus V1 remains an elution interval. The expected benefit is better structure–condition interpolation, endpoint-specific transfer and use of loading features across the Row-distribution after retraining.
